facts.text: Port Alexander was named in 1849 by Russian Captain Mikhail Dmitrievich Tebenkov, likely honoring Governor Alexander Andreyevich Baranov.
Before European contact, the area that is now Port Alexander was part of Tlingit territory, where salmon fishing was central to their culture.
In the early 20th century, Port Alexander was one of Alaska’s important fishing ports, with hundreds of trolling boats catching over 5 million pounds of salmon annually.
In 1928, Karl Hansen received a license for a wireless telegraphy station, making Port Alexander the first place in the area to connect to the outside world.
In 1930 Congress funded a 150‑foot wide, 15‑foot deep channel from Chatham Strait into Port Alexander, opening the harbor for larger vessels.
The Port Alexander Historical Society, founded in 1995, opened a museum in 2010 that preserves the town’s fishing heritage and the home of early settler Karl Hansen.
